answer.generated: To determine the number of processors with the highest speedup in an application where P% of the original execution time is parallelizable, and the communication cost increases by 0.5% of the original execution time for every doubling of the number of processors, one must consider the balance between parallelizable work and communication overhead. The speedup \( S \) can be expressed as \( S = \frac{P}{(1 - P/2^n)} \), where \( n \) represents the number of times the number of processors has been doubled. The highest speedup occurs when the communication overhead equals the parallelizable work, i.e., when \( P/2^n = 0.5\% \cdot P \). Solving for \( n \) yields the optimal number of doublings, which corresponds to the number of processors with the highest speedup.
